2607.22376.title: A Factorial Study of Synthetic Data Generation for Low-Resource Machine Translation using Grammar Books
2607.22376.paper_summary: Most endangered languages lack the parallel data required for machine translation, despite the existence of descriptive grammar books. We introduce a pipeline that uses large language models to extract grammatical rules, example sentences, and lexicons from grammar books and generate synthetic parallel corpora for fine-tuning-rather than feeding grammar content into prompts at inference time, as in prior work. Validated on three typologically diverse low-resource languages-Kalamang (Papuan), Tuatschin (Romance), and Mandan (Siouan)-we show that fine-tuning on synthetic data improves over seed-data baselines in 75% of configurations for Kalamang and 59% for Tuatschin, with best-case ChrF++ gains of +8.8, +5.3, and +3.3 respectively. Through a systematic factorial study across 96 configurations varying target part-of-speech, retrieval granularity, and sample volume, we identify which factor combinations drive gains and where they break down. Our results demonstrate that static linguistic documentation can be repurposed for machine translation fine-tuning, offering a practical path towards translation tools for severely under-resourced languages.
2607.22376.paper_summary_zh: 大多數瀕危語言缺乏機器翻譯所需的平行數據，儘管存在描述性語法書。我們介紹了一個管道，利用大型語言模型從語法書中提取語法規則、示例句子和詞彙，並生成合成平行語料庫進行微調——而不是像之前的工作那樣在推理時將語法內容輸入提示中。我們在三種類型學上多樣的低資源語言上進行驗證——卡拉曼語（Papuan）、圖阿奇語（Romance）和曼丹語（Siouan）——顯示在合成數據上進行微調在75%的配置中對卡拉曼語和59%的配置中對圖阿奇語改善了種子數據基準，最佳情況下ChrF++的增益分別為+8.8、+5.3和+3.3。通過在96個配置中進行系統的因子研究，變化目標詞性、檢索粒度和樣本量，我們確定了哪些因子組合驅動增益以及它們在哪裡失效。我們的結果表明，靜態語言學文獻可以重新用於機器翻譯微調，為嚴重資源不足的語言提供了一條實用的翻譯工具之路。
